rationale:
Evidence: the best raced design is iteration 7 (score 49.95): 5 sensors at y = 0.06 m, x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, 0.016 m footprint, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, kp 2.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.4, search_right. Every trial in every iteration ended off track with exactly one line-loss event, and max_error is censored near 0.061 m by the 0.06 m limit. Iterations 0 and 2 gave identical per-track metrics across large kp, kd and ki changes, so gains did not reach the first loss. Iteration 6 (kd 0.05 instead of 0.1) fell from 49.94 to 35.65, so kd matters somewhat even though it does not set the first loss.

Critique assessment. Accepted: the round-1 draft changed too many things at once. Its geometry (7 sensors, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.14) and its kp, kd and base_speed were not isolated, so no result could be attributed. Accepted: kd 0.6 is about 6 times the raced value and, at a 0.5 signal step per 10 ms, risks saturating the wheels, so kd returns to the raced 0.1. Accepted: the critique is right that a 2% motor mismatch is only about 0.12 turn units, and that the integral's timing before the first loss is unchecked. Partly accepted: the ki test is still worth running, because it is the only untested term that could counter the fixed left/right bias, and the integral clamp of +/-2 bounds its effect. I do not accept the claim that ki 0.1 to 0.3 was a null test over the whole run, since it was confounded with other changes. Rejected: I keep base_speed at 1.4, since changing speed now would confound the ki test, and I do not claim completion.

Change (one variable from iteration 7): ki 0.1 to 1.0. The integral clamp gives up to 2 turn units (about 700 PWM), which is enough to cancel a steady bias if the bias is the cause. Everything else matches iteration 7.

Expected result (a guess, labelled as such): if a steady bias drives the first loss, the first-loss step should move later or disappear, and progress should rise on the oval and s-bend. If the first loss is unchanged, the integral is not reaching a useful size before the loss, and the cause is the start condition or the recovery rule.

Decision rule for the next round: if the first-loss step and progress at first loss are unchanged, set ki back to 0.1 and test start handling with geometry and gains fixed. If the loss moves later and progress rises, keep ki 1.0 and check whether the integral windup shows up as steering_oscillation. If max_error and oscillation rise together, drop ki to about 0.3. Read first-loss timing and progress at first loss, not max_error, because failed runs are censored at 0.061 m.
